clue.text: Surprise Gene Hackman, say, by beginning to twerk

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: Gene Hackman is an example of a film star
first letter of twerk

explanation.surface: A Hollywood veteran is startled by someone launching into a twerk.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump with sudden fright, so the verb is a synonym of surprise used intransitively or as a noun.

clue.text: Did notice used to be up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: first sense: past tense of see
past tense of the verb to be

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing that once stood upright was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a true double definition: the second half is wordplay, the past tense of to be written upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb see means observed or noticed something.

clue.text: Great teacher that's noble felt upset, having banished fellow

indicators.note: banishing someone sends them away, so the named letter is dropped from the word before it
upset means turned over, and in a down entry the letters then read upwards

blocks.note: informal shortening of aristocrat
taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster with titled connections is hurt after a colleague is expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher taught Alexander the Great and is a byword for a great teacher of antiquity.

clue.text: Maybe Mr T's gripped by part of Scrabble game

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Scrabble is played with lettered tiles
taken as written from Mr T's

explanation.surface: The A-Team actor Mr T is somehow caught up in a game of Scrabble.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr T is a real person, but here 'Mr' alone is the definition and the T is the letter that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr is an honorific placed before a name, which is one kind of title, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Competitive drunk that drinks limitless grog

indicators.note: a drinker takes something in, so one word holds the other within it
without limits means the outer letters are lost and only the inner part is kept

blocks.note: cut is British slang for tipsy
taken as written
grog without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boozer who is sipping a rum mix is fiercely competitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-throat competition is ruthless and merciless, so the adjective describes extreme rivalry.

clue.text: With bottom raised, pop singer devours cheese

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom letter is the last, and raising it moves it to the top
what is devoured ends up inside, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: Cher is the American pop singer
pop is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A pop star bending over eats some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like part of 'pop singer', but it is a father, whose last letter moves to the front before Cher swallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard cheese named after the Somerset village where it originated.

clue.text: Victory one sealed with card of the best suit – hearts

indicators.note: something sealed in is enclosed, so one letter sits inside the card

blocks.note: a trump is a card of the suit that beats all others
Roman numeral one
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card notation

explanation.surface: A card player wins by holding the top suit, which happens to be hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great success or win, a direct synonym of victory.

clue.text: Sleep with two-thirds of Scottish football team at the back of Travelodge

indicators.note: taking two-thirds of a nine-letter name keeps six letters and drops the final three
the back of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: Hibernian is an Edinburgh football club
taken as written
last letter of Travelodge

explanation.surface: Most of a Scottish football side crash out at the back of a budget hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Travelodge is a British chain of budget hotels; Hibernian, often called Hibs, plays in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: To hibernate is to pass the winter in a dormant state, a long seasonal sleep.

clue.text: Movement of large body or small particle

blocks.note: taken as written
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A physics question contrasting how planets move with how tiny particles move.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the curved path a planet or moon follows around a larger celestial body.

clue.text: Empty trinkets fitted with lead and steel and covered in tiles

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving just the outer letters
fitted together means assembled into a new arrangement

blocks.note: trinkets with its inside removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Metal trinkets are mounted with lead and steel to make a decorative tiled object.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessellated surface is laid as a mosaic of small square pieces, as a tiled floor is.

clue.text: One's played card game with 50 naked men

indicators.note: stripped naked means the outer covering goes, so only the middle survives

blocks.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
Roman numeral fifty
men without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fifty men with no clothes on sit down to a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's played' reads as part of the card-game story, but it is the definition: something one plays, as a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is a simple wind instrument, and instruments are things that are played.

clue.text: Solomon goes with male and female workers, half-heartedly getting drinks

indicators.note: halving the heart of a word loses one of its two middle letters

blocks.note: the setter is Solomon, who refers to himself as I
M is the abbreviation for male
short for bisexual, attracted to both male and female
worker bees, which are female

explanation.surface: The setter teams up with a mixed group of staff, who end up having drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Solomon is this puzzle's setter, so his name gives I. BI is read from 'male and female', with 'male' doing double duty, a loose element in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol, so the third-person form matches the verb drinks.

clue.text: City wall by which rat is seen

blocks.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a rotter
a dam is a wall holding back water

explanation.surface: A rat is spotted beside a city wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major port city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Mobile young students entering on time for snacks

definitions.note: plural noun defining a singular, used as a mass noun

indicators.note: entering means going in, so the students sit inside the other letters

T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: First-year students on the move turn up just in time for snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like an anagram signal but is the Alabama city, marking freshmen as an American term for new students.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshment covers light food and drink served to people, so it can stand for snacks collectively.

clue.text: Before match, men gather again

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a common crossword source for men
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Before a game the players assemble once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before match' tells the solver the men go in front of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to tie up once more, and gathering something up with string is tying it.

clue.text: Units Tesla shifted at small festivals

indicators.note: the tesla is a unit whose symbol is moved within the word, rearranging it

blocks.note: feet are units of length
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Electric cars from Tesla are moved about at small local festivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density with symbol T, so the T in the units moves one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising fair, the plural naming small local festivals.

clue.text: Upstanding American supported by a woman's love for one with power

indicators.note: standing up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: abbreviation of United States
per means a, as in once a day
possessive pronoun for a woman
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An honest American is backed by a woman who loves a powerful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supported by' in a down clue means the next pieces sit underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero is a fictional character with special powers, such as flight or great strength.

clue.text: Half of Alan Shearer's shot practice

something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: first half of Alan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shot taken by footballer Alan Shearer is merely a training exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England striker; 'shot' suggests football, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a trial performance done as practice before the real event.

clue.text: Even now, animation is a form of drawing

blocks.note: still means even now, up to this time
animation in the sense of liveliness or life

explanation.surface: A remark that animation still counts as a kind of drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Animation suggests cartoons, which fits drawing, but here it means being alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is an artwork depicting inanimate objects, often a drawing or painting of fruit or flowers.

clue.text: The old, old writer drawn in by English queen that lifts the lid

definitions.note: verb phrase defining a noun: a thing that lifts the lid

indicators.note: drawn in means pulled inside, so the earlier pieces sit within the outer ones

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
ye is an archaic form of the
O is the abbreviation for old
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: An ancient author is sketched by an English queen in a revealing portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, and to lift the lid on something is to expose it.

clue.text: Easy quality of life for Prince Andrew?

definitions.text: quality of life for Prince Andrew

blocks.note: first meaning: no trouble at all

blocks.clueFragment: quality of life for Prince Andrew
blocks.note: second meaning: a reference to Prince Andrew's 2019 TV claim that he could not perspire

explanation.walkthrough: In a 2019 BBC interview Prince Andrew said a medical condition left him unable to perspire; the second half takes the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means something presents no difficulty, a colloquial synonym for easy.

clue.text: Unusual black Italian dish

B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An odd, dark Italian recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian dish' looks like one phrase, but the dish is Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury dish of melted cheese sauce on toast.

clue.text: Are leaves turning? Only at the end

clue.text: Who wrote great verses in Radiohead?

read as Radio head: the first letter of Radio

clue.text: Damp cloud surrounding the top of Olympus

blocks.note: mist is low-lying cloud
first letter of Olympus

explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, a direct synonym of damp.

clue.text: Climbed on your bike, exhausted

clue.text: Dummy supporting rubbish hat in Spitalfields

clue.text: Fabric from cute dolly's face
